name: Artisans Asylum
accessSummary: Open to the public via membership or day passes after a free New Member Orientation and tool testing. 24/7 membership $250/mo ($225/mo annual); Days & Weekends or Nights & Weekends $150/mo; Student $130/mo; Co-working $70/mo; Family $350/mo; Day Pass $40 (10-pack $300). Classes are open to non-members.
foundedNote: Opened May 2010 in Somerville; moved to the Holton St./Antwerp St. campus in Allston-Brighton in 2022–2023.
hours: Members: 24/7 key-fob access. Front desk (non-member entry): Mon–Thu 10am–4pm. Public tours Tue 6pm, Fri 12pm, Sat 11am.
equipment: Laser cutters (DigiFab shop)
Formlabs SLA resin printer system
Prusa, Bambu, and Creality FDM 3D printers
ShopBot large-format CNC router
CNC plasma cutter
SawStop 5HP ICS table saws
15" jointer and 15" bandsaw (wood shop)
Manual and CNC mills and lathes (machine shop)
Metal shop with welding, cutting, and grinding; sandblasting and powder coating studio
Sand casting and investment casting shop
Jewelry shop with glass enamel studio
Domestic and industrial sewing machines (fiber arts)
Screen printing exposure, curing, and washout equipment
Paint booth (finishing shop)
Electronics and robotics bench; bike shop (SCUL)
description: Artisans Asylum is a nonprofit community makerspace founded in Somerville in 2010 and now based on a two-building campus in Allston-Brighton. It offers memberships, day passes, classes, and rentable private studios across roughly 17 shared shops spanning woodworking, metalworking, digital fabrication, electronics, textiles, jewelry, casting, and screen printing. Members get 24/7 access after orientation and tool testing.

name: gather here
accessSummary: Open to the public. Studio space (sewing machine, cutting table, irons, tools) rents for $10/hour with a discounted all-day block, bookable online. The BERNINA Q24 longarm rents for $20/hr and the sit-down Q20 for $10/hr (2-hour minimum; Longarm Basics class required first).
foundedNote: Opened February 2011 at 370 Broadway, Cambridge; moved to Inman Square about five years later (founder interview, secondary source).
hours: Shop: Mon–Thu 12–8:30pm; Fri–Sun 11am–6pm. Dedicated studio hours: Mon 12–8pm, Wed 5:30–8:30pm, Fri 11am–6pm, Sat 1–4:30pm (other times by arrangement).
equipment: BERNINA sewing machines (studio stations)
Six sergers / coverstitch machines
BERNINA Q24 longarm quilting machine (on frame)
BERNINA Q20 sit-down longarm quilting machine
Cutting tables, irons, and ironing stations
36"-wide large-format printer for PDF sewing patterns
Downstairs wet work space with six machines and a sink (for parties and workshops)
description: gather here is an independently owned fabric and yarn shop and "stitch lounge" in Inman Square that rents studio time on BERNINA sewing machines, sergers, and longarm quilting machines. It runs sewing, knitting, crochet, embroidery, and quilting classes, prints large-format PDF patterns, and offers in-house sewing machine repair as an authorized BERNINA dealer.

name: Medford MakerSpace & Tech Lab (Medford Public Library)
accessSummary: Open to all at no cost. Take the free General Safety badge class and sign a waiver to reserve the MakerSpace or Tech Lab independently, plus equipment-specific badge classes (laser cutter, 3D printer, Cricut, sewing machine, serger). Drop-in hours need no badge or registration. 3D printing costs $0.10 per gram.
eligibility: Open to all; badges for independent use for adults and minors 16+ with a caregiver-signed waiver; ages 8+ with active adult supervision
foundedNote: Approximate. Funded by a May 2021 Cummings Foundation grant for the new Charlotte and William Bloomberg Medford Public Library building, which opened in early 2022.
hours: Reservable (badged) hours Mon–Thu 9am–8:30pm, Fri 9am–5:30pm, Sat 9am–4:30pm; drop-in Mon 6–8pm and Fri 4–5:30pm
equipment: Glowforge Pro laser cutter
MakerBot Sketch 3D printers (2)
Dremel DigiLab 3D45 3D printer
Bambu Lab X1-Carbon 3D printer with AMS (coming soon)
Cricut Maker with EasyPress and Mug Press
Genmitsu 3018-PROVer CNC router (coming soon)
Brother CS7000X and Janome 2212 sewing machines
Baby Lock Victory serger
Soldering stations (5) with fume extractor
Dremel rotary tool, Moto-Saw, and cordless drills
Button press (2.25 in)
Recording studio with Mac, PreSonus mic/interface, and MIDI keyboards
LEGO EV3, Ozobots, and littleBits robotics kits
description: The Medford MakerSpace and Tech Lab are two public rooms in the Charlotte and William Bloomberg Medford Public Library stocked with a laser cutter, 3D printers, a Cricut, sewing and serger machines, soldering stations, hand and power tools, and an acoustically insulated recording studio. The spaces are free to use after a General Safety badge class, with regular drop-in hours and classes for ages 8 and up.

name: Nolop FAST Facility (Tufts)
accessSummary: Free for anyone with a Tufts ID. Walk in and ask staff at the desk for help. Most tools can be used after reading basic instructions; the supervised "red zone" woodworking tools require Nolop safety training.
eligibility: Tufts students, faculty, and staff (anyone with a Tufts ID)
address: Science and Engineering Complex, 200 College Avenue, Medford, MA 02155
foundedNote: Opened January 2019, funded by a gift from the estate of Keith Nolop.
hours: Fall/spring: Mon–Thu 9am–11pm; Fri 9am–6pm; Sun 9am–11pm; Sat usually closed. Summer: weekdays 9am–5pm. Closed between terms.
equipment: Universal VLS 3.60 laser cutter
Prusa i3 MK3 3D printer farm
Inventables X-Carve 750mm CNC router
SawStop ICS table saw
Laguna 18CX vertical bandsaw
Powermatic PM2800B drill press
DeWalt miter saw and scroll saw
Tennsmith sheet metal shear and brake
Rigol MSO5074 oscilloscope
Hakko FX951 soldering stations
Proxxon hot wire foam cutter
Cordless drills, jigsaw, circular saw, router, and hand tools
description: Nolop (officially the Nolop FAST Facility) is Tufts University's makerspace, opened in January 2019 in the basement of the Science and Engineering Complex. It is free for anyone with a Tufts ID and provides laser cutting, 3D printing, CNC routing, woodworking, sheet-metal, and electronics tools, with staff on hand to teach safe use. The more dangerous woodworking tools sit in a supervised "red zone" with a posted schedule.

name: REEF Makerspace (Harvard SEAS)
accessSummary: Free for active Harvard community members (students, staff, and faculty with a valid HUID) after a 20-minute in-person orientation and the EHS online safety training; swipe access follows within about a week. Alumni, spouses, guests, and minors are not admitted. Laser, woodshop, and CNC use requires additional training.
eligibility: Harvard students, staff, and faculty with a valid HUID
address: Science and Engineering Complex, Room 1.112, 150 Western Avenue, Allston, MA 02134
foundedNote: Opening year not stated on official pages. The SEC building opened in 2021 and SEAS news about the REEF Makerspace begins in 2023.
hours: Swipe access: Sun–Thu 6am–2am; Fri 6am–5pm; Sat closed. Staffed hours vary by semester.
equipment: Epilog Fusion Edge and Epilog Fusion Pro laser cutters
Prusa MK4S, Prusa Core One L, and Snapmaker U1 FDM 3D printers
CNC routers including Carvera Air and Shapeoko 5 Pro
Woodshop: vertical bandsaw, drill press, belt/disc sander, scroll saw, compound miter saw, panel saw, cabinet router
Electronics station: soldering stations, power supplies, oscilloscopes, waveform generators
Sewing machine, serger, CNC embroidery machine, and Cricut vinyl cutter
Casting room / spray booth: thermoformer, spray paint booth, oven, fume hood, pressure pot
Dye sublimation printer and heat press
Photo booth with DSLR camera, studio lighting, and backdrops
Meta Quest 3 headset and handheld 3D scanners
Bike and skateboard repair stand and tooling
description: The REEF Makerspace (Reimagining Experiential Education & Fabrication) is Harvard SEAS's makerspace on the first floor of the Science and Engineering Complex in Allston. It gives Harvard students, staff, and faculty access to laser cutters, FDM 3D printers, CNC routers, a woodshop, electronics benches, fabric arts tools, and a casting/spray booth, supported by staff and student Maker Fellows.

name: The Hive at Cambridge Public Library
accessSummary: Free with a Minuteman Library Network card. Complete the free Hive Safety Training (a 10-minute video during Open Shop or a scheduled class), sign the user agreement, then take badging workshops for specific equipment and reserve tools or studios online, by phone, or in person.
eligibility: Minuteman Library Network cardholders; independent use ages 12+, supervised use for children under 12
foundedNote: Opened July 6, 2021 on the lower level (L2) of the Main Library.
hours: Varies; Open Shop sessions several times a week (weekday afternoons/evenings and Saturdays). See the calendar.
equipment: Epilog Zing 16 laser cutter
Epilog Fusion Maker laser cutter (coming soon)
Prusa MK3S 3D printer
Roland CAMM-1 GS-24 vinyl cutter
Cricut Maker
Janome MyStyle 100 sewing machines
Elna eXtend 864 Air serger
Digital embroidery machine
Multimedia recording studio
Podcasting studio
Extended reality (XR) lab with AR/VR equipment
Software: Adobe Creative Suite, GarageBand, iMovie, CorelDRAW, Inkscape, FL Studio
description: The Hive is the Cambridge Public Library's free STEAM makerspace on the lower level of the Main Library, with a fabrication lab, multimedia and podcasting studios, and an extended reality lab. After a short safety training and equipment badging workshops, cardholders can reserve tools and studios during Open Shop hours.
